description: One mind. One vision. One orbit.
summary: EarthPulse helps students and curious members of the public explore how near-surface air temperature changes over time. It connects NASA MERRA-2 data, delivered by POWER, with a coordinate locator, an annual time-series chart, descriptive trend estimates and fixed-period comparisons. Users can download annual and monthly CSVs, full-precision results with provenance, and an evidence brief. Tested uncertainty methods did not meet preset calibration criteria. The app reports descriptive trends and withholds significance claims, confidence intervals and p-values pending validated inference.
details:
Quiet Orbit developed EarthPulse. Sirena Gazale led the project and contributed requirements and source review, development, implementation review and manual testing. Fande Gazale contributed web development and hands-on testing.

EarthPulse explores NASA POWER/MERRA-2 near-surface air temperature at three requested locations. It displays the 2001–2024 annual record, compares two fixed 20-year windows (2001–2020 and 2005–2024), and offers anomalies relative to a custom 2001–2020 baseline. Users can inspect the plotted values in an accessible table and export CSV, results with provenance in JSON, or an evidence brief in Markdown.

Python validates timestamps, units, missing data and source hashes. It separates source annual summaries from monthly values and computes calendar-day-weighted annual means. OLS estimates the descriptive trend in °C per decade, with Theil–Sen as a descriptive comparison. React, TypeScript and Vite deliver the precomputed results through a responsive static app.

The data are grid-scale reanalysis estimates. Native-cell identity is unverified. Calibration tests for HAC, AR(1) GLS/REML and bootstrap-t failed preset criteria. Inference remains unvalidated, and the app provides no confidence intervals, p-values, causal claims or forecasts.

ChatGPT and OpenAI Codex assisted proposal discussions, source review, implementation, tests, documentation and presentation. The app uses deterministic explanations. NASA data are authentic archived reanalysis estimates, and the validation simulations are separate. Prior feasibility artifacts and AI-assisted proposal work are disclosed; their eligibility remains subject to organizer interpretation.
